patients.summary: Healthy 32-year-old business development manager who joins the practice in July 2025 with cryptosporidiosis after a work trip to southern Mexico. Later seen at two outside EDs: dehydration at a Florida marathon in January 2026 and norovirus with dehydration on a cruise in July 2026. Otherwise routine preventive care.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, new patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT, ACUTE

CC: watery diarrhea for 6 days.

HPI: 32F, joined the practice this week. Got home roughly a week ago from ten days in southern Mexico for work. A lot of the trip was outdoor events, and she ate street food and drank local drinks there. Diarrhea began about 6 days ago; watery, as many as 8 times a day, with mild crampy belly pain. Never any blood or mucus, no tenesmus. No vomiting. No fever. Eating less than usual and wiped out, but says she has kept fluids up fine. Hasn't taken anything for it.

PMH: none. Healthy, no immune problems.
PSH: tonsillectomy at 12; wisdom teeth out at 21.
Meds: none.
Allergies: NKDA.
FHx: mother hypothyroid. Father HTN. No immunodeficiency or GI disease in the family.
SH: international business development, travels a fair amount. Married. Never smoker. Drinks socially, 1-2 a week. Runs for exercise.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet, afebrile. Looks tired. Mucous membranes dry. Neck supple. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, mildly tender diffusely, no guarding or rebound, normal bowel sounds, no hepatosplenomegaly. Skin warm, no rash.

A/P:
1. Acute watery diarrhea after travel to southern Mexico, day 6, nonbloody, afebrile. Mildly dry on exam but drinking. Bacterial pathogens vs parasite (crypto, cyclospora, giardia). Sending stool culture and modified acid-fast stain. BMP and CBC today.
- Oral rehydration: ORS or broth plus salty crackers, aim to keep urine pale.
- Hold off on loperamide until we know what this is.
- Call or text same day for blood in stool, fever, or not keeping fluids down.
2. Health maintenance: get prior records in, full physical in the fall.

Follow-up: will call with stool results.

documents.title: Your blood work from today
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Lauren, your electrolytes and kidney numbers came back normal, so the fluids are keeping up. Your white count is slightly high, which fits with a gut infection and isn't worrying by itself. Stool tests take a couple of days. I'll call you when they're in.

documents.title: Stool Results Call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt with stool results. Culture: no bacterial pathogens. Modified AFB stain positive, oocysts c/w Cryptosporidium. Explained the diagnosis: a parasite picked up from food or water, usually clears on its own in 1-3 weeks in someone healthy. She is still having 5-6 watery stools a day, cramping a bit better, drinking well, no fever. Plan supportive: fluids/ORS, normal diet as tolerated. It spreads easily, so careful handwashing, don't cook for others while symptomatic, and no pools or hot tubs until 2 weeks after the diarrhea stops. She will message if not improving in a week or if she can't keep up with fluids.

documents.title: Feeling better
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Quick update, the diarrhea finally stopped around Saturday the 9th and I've been eating normally since. Back in the office this week. Is there anything I need to do now or am I all set? Thanks!

documents.title: RE: Feeling better
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glad to hear it. Nothing more to do. No need to retest. Just stay out of pools until about the 23rd. We'll see you for your physical in October.

reports.text: Specimen: ThinPrep, satisfactory for evaluation; transformation zone component present. Interpretation: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. High-risk HPV: not detected.

- Problem list: none active.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL PHYSICAL

S: 32F here for her first full physical with us. Feels well. The cryptosporidium in July-August cleared in about two weeks without treatment and bowels have been normal since. Running 4-5 days a week, working up toward a marathon this winter. Travels for work every month or two. Sleep okay. Periods regular. No concerns today.

PMH: cryptosporidiosis 7-8/2025, resolved.
PSH: tonsillectomy age 12; third molars age 21.
Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
FHx: mom hypothyroidism; dad hypertension.
SH: married, works in international business development. Never smoked. Alcohol 1-2 drinks/week.

ROS: negative x 12 systems.

O: Vitals reviewed. Well, fit-appearing. HEENT: TMs clear, oropharynx normal, tonsils surgically absent. Neck: no thyroid enlargement, no lymphadenopathy. CV: RRR, no murmurs. Lungs: clear bilaterally. Abd: soft, nontender, no masses. Ext: no edema. Skin: no concerning lesions. Neuro: grossly nonfocal. Mood/affect normal.

PHQ-2: 0.

A/P: Healthy adult, preventive visit.
- Pap/HPV co-test 3/2023 normal at prior office, next due 2028.
- Tdap 2018, good until 2028.
- Flu vaccine given today. Offered this season's COVID shot, she'll think about it.
- One-time HIV and hep C screens, CBC (recheck the white count from July), CMP, lipids.
- Hydration and fueling on long runs, especially when traveling somewhere hot.
RTC 1 year, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Vaccine Administration
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Influenza vaccine 0.5 mL IM left deltoid. Standard pre-vaccine questions answered, no contraindications. VIS provided. Tolerated without issue, observed 15 min.
